# Generated by rules/link.sh. Do not edit this file.

Edit files in `rules/` and run `rules/link.sh`.

# Start

- Before you edit anything, run
  `node tools/agent-context.mjs <paths you will touch>` and read every file
  that it lists.
- Restate the task against those rules before your first edit.
- If the task conflicts with a rule or with a decision record, stop and ask
  the owner. Do not work around it.

# Communication

- Do not use em dash or en dash characters.
- Write user-facing text in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
- Start status reports with the result, then give the evidence.

# Git and GitHub

- Use conventional commits.
- Never force push.
- Do not use a bare `#N` in a GitHub comment or pull request body. Write
  `item 1`, `(2)`, or a plain list. Use `#NNNN` only for a real pull request or
  issue.
- Work happens in a git worktree on a short-lived branch.
- A change lands through a protected GitHub pull request and merge queue.
  Required hosted Check and Sign-off results prove the selected source.
  Resolve every review thread. Review is optional (record 0218).
  No actor bypasses protection. Never push a change directly to main.
- A build request includes landing only when the session permits it.
  It never permits release or live deployment.
- A pull request shows its screenshots through `tools/pr-screenshots.mjs`,
  which adds them to the `pr-screenshots` branch. Never delete that branch.
- Stay inside the active worktree. All edits, commits, and untracked files
  belong in that worktree.
- Only the owner starts the `cleaning-up-after-a-task` skill. Never run it on
  your own, and never remove another worktree, another branch, or Docker data
  outside it.
- Follow the `release-core` skill for an explicit release request.
  Release is unavailable during the transition to the hosted workflow
  (record 0228). The old commands are removed in step 4 of issue 390.
  A pushed signed tag is never moved and never deleted.

# Product design

- Read `docs/development/design.md` before you change anything a person sees.
  It is the one system, and `tools/check-design-rules.mjs` holds its rules.
- Use Tailwind CSS utilities for application layout and presentation.
- Do not add handwritten CSS selectors, CSS modules, component style sheets,
  or inline `style` properties.
- `apps/web/src/tailwind.css` is the only application CSS source. It can have
  only Tailwind imports, source registration, central theme variables, and the
  `@font-face` rules of a vendored face (0061). No other file declares a face
  or names a family.
- One family, Geist, for everything a person reads, and Geist Mono for code
  and a keyboard hint (0061).
- Keep color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadow decisions in the central
  Tailwind theme and runtime palette. Do not add arbitrary Tailwind values.
- Color comes from the theme registry in `packages/ui/src/themes` only. Do not
  write a color value anywhere else. A new theme is one data file plus one
  registry entry.
- The one filled action on a screen is the primary button, and it appears once.
  The accent text colour marks a link, a focus ring, a caret and a selection
  and nothing else (0062).
- Use the named type steps only: `text-kbd`, `text-control`, `text-ui`,
  `text-base`, `text-xl`, `text-3xl` and the note steps. Two weights,
  `font-medium` and `font-semibold`. No capitals, no wide tracking.
- Every page is the note column (record 0137). Only the home page of the
  landing site may use `max-w-5xl`, a `text-3xl` hero headline, a 20 px feature
  icon, and a real screenshot in `rounded-lg`, `edge-subtle` and
  `shadow-overlay` (record 0217).
- Use the standard Tailwind spacing scale. Do not add one-off pixel or rem
  spacing values.
- `edge-line` is the resting edge of a control and the one divider. `edge` is
  only a task box, a checkbox, a radio, a switch and a drop target (0063).
  Separate with space and fill before a line.
- Every control reads its classes from `packages/ui/src/control-classes.ts`.
  No screen writes the classes of a button, a row, a field or a hint (0065).
- An icon is 16 px in a control and a row, 20 px in an empty state, from the
  one set at a stroke of 1.5. An icon-only action has a `label` (0065).
- Radius: `rounded-md` on a control and a row, `rounded-lg` on a card, a menu
  and a toast, `rounded-xl` on a dialog, `rounded-sm` on a hint and a task box.
- A typed adapter for a third-party rendering system, such as CodeMirror, can
  set presentation in TypeScript only when utility classes cannot reach its
  generated DOM. It must use the central Tailwind and semantic theme variables.
- Use native semantic elements. Every icon-only action must have an accessible
  name and a title when the purpose is not clear from context.
- Keep keyboard focus visible with the one focus treatment. Dialogs must
  support Escape. Important actions must be possible without a pointer.
- Use compact controls by default. Keep controls large enough for reliable
  pointer and touch input.
- Take a screenshot in light and in dark before a screen lands.

# Application architecture

- Keep package boundaries strict. Domain code must not import transport,
  database, browser, or React code.
- Use generated API client operations. Do not write request URLs or direct
  `fetch` calls in feature code.
- Treat browser drafts as recovery data, not server versions. Only a
  checkpoint creates an immutable server version: a pause in typing, leaving
  the note, or Ctrl + S (decision record 0022).
- Keep one CodeMirror editor instance for an open working copy. Do not replace
  its document during a React render, theme change, or preview update.
- Store note paths with one `.md` suffix. Hide this storage detail from the
  person who edits the note name.
- Keep rich Markdown rendering isolated from network and storage access. Pass
  attachments and diagram rendering through typed resolvers.
- Validate at domain boundaries. Do not weaken a server invariant to hide a
  client defect.
- Put new code where decision record 0018 says. It states the directory
  structure of the server, `core`, the stores, and the web application.
- Do not write a type assertion. Only `as const` is allowed. Reach a type
  through a type guard or a parser that fails loudly (decision record 0019).
- Before a change to the interface that a service of the operator depends on,
  read `docs/development/operator-api.md`. It names that interface and the
  changes that break it. When a checkout of the cloud repository sits beside
  this one at `../cloud`, read its `AGENTS.md` too, and state the effect on
  the cloud in the commit body. `tools/agent-context.mjs` lists both files.

# Verification

- Add a regression test for each fixed defect.
- A change of source carries a test of its area (record 0154).
  `tools/check-change-tests.mjs` runs in `pnpm lint` and as the Stop hook of
  `.claude/settings.json`, and it refuses a branch that changes the source of
  a package or a tool and no test of it. When a change cannot have a test,
  state why in a commit trailer: `Test-exempt: <area> <reason>`.
- Prove what a person sees through the pure module that decides it and through
  an integration test of the served result.
- Take a screenshot of each changed screen in light and in dark before a
  landing.
- To run the application of a worktree and drive it in a browser, follow the
  `test-application` skill. Each worktree runs its own application,
  so worktrees do not conflict.
- Run focused tests while work is in progress. Required hosted checks prove
  the change before merge. Local `pnpm verify` is an optional diagnostic.
- Do not weaken assertions, add fixed delays, or skip a failing test to make a
  suite pass.

# Feature workflow

- Before you edit under a directory, read its `AGENTS.md`. Every app, every
  package, and the `tests` tree has one.
- Follow `docs/development/feature-workflow.md` for a whole feature. The
  order is the contract, the domain rule, the storage, the handler, the
  client, then the verification.
- Write the operation in `packages/api-contract/` before any code that uses
  it, then run `pnpm generate`. One file holds one path item and one file
  holds one component. `openapi.yaml` is the root that lists them. Never edit
  a file under a `src/generated/` directory.
- A new architectural choice gets a decision record in `docs/decisions`
  before the code. A choice is architectural when it moves a boundary, adds
  or removes a package, changes the save model, adds a second parser or
  renderer, changes the contract emit rules, changes the migration policy, or
  changes what the verification gate proves.
- Keep `AGENTS.md` true. A change that moves a boundary, a key file, or a
  rule updates the `AGENTS.md` of that directory in the same commit.

# User-facing text

- Write every word a person reads in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English:
  one idea per sentence, the active voice, the present tense, and a short
  approved word.
- Use sentence case for a label, a heading, a button, and a menu item. Keep a
  product name and a key name in their own case.
- Never show an identifier, a path suffix, a digest, a raw timestamp, an
  error code, a stack, or an engine notice. Show the name, the relative time,
  and the action that helps.
- Give one message for one cause. Do not stack a general message and a
  detailed message for the same failure.
- A message states what happened and what the person can do next. It does not
  blame the person and it does not apologize.
- Handle the plural with a count and a whole phrase, for example `1 note` and
  `3 notes`. Do not append a bare `(s)`.
- Name an empty state by what is missing and offer the one action that fills
  it.
- Keep one term for one thing across the whole application: Save, Trash,
  Restore, Delete, History, Read, Write. In Trash, the page copy states that
  Delete removes a note for good.

# Documents

- Before you write a document, read `docs/README.md`. It states the audience,
  the purpose, and the required header of each documentation directory.
- A document points at code by path and never copies it. Do not copy source, a
  configuration value, a schema, a column list, SQL, TypeScript, YAML, a
  version number, or a measured result.
- The one allowed code block is a shell command that the reader runs, in `sh`,
  `bash` or `shell`. A block with no language or with any other language
  fails `pnpm lint`, except in a document whose status line says that it is
  superseded.
- Every `.md` file under `docs/` sits in `guide`, `development`, `design`,
  `decisions`, `audits`, or `plans`.
- A file in `docs/plans/` or `docs/design/` carries `Status: active`,
  `Status: complete`, or `Status: superseded by <relative link>` directly under
  its title.
- `docs/guide/` is public and flat. Each page starts with the title line and
  one sentence that states who the page is for.
- `docs/development/` holds the intent, the invariants, and the pointers of one
  area. Keep a page under 150 lines. Link a decision record rather than
  restating the decision.
- A new architectural choice gets a record in `docs/decisions/` from the
  template, before the code.
- The [GitHub project board](https://github.com/users/bkhanale/projects/2) is
  the one prioritized list of open work. See `docs/development/tracking.md`. The
  repository holds no release list.
- An audit in `docs/audits/<date>/` names its date and its commit and is never
  edited after it lands.
- A document that no longer describes the product stays with its kind. Set its
  status to superseded and point at the document that replaced it. Do not edit
  it again, except its status line.

A large task runs through five stages:

1. A design in `docs/design/` states the problem, the options, and the cost of
   each option. Write it in prose for a person who reads it once.
2. The design concludes in one or more records in `docs/decisions/`. The design
   and each record link each other.
3. A plan in `docs/plans/` turns those records into ordered work, and links the
   design and the records. Write it terse, structured, and full of pointers,
   for an agent that loads it many times.
4. The rows of the plan become issues on the
   [GitHub project board](https://github.com/users/bkhanale/projects/2), one row
   per issue, each with a milestone, a priority label, and an area label.
5. When the plan completes, its status becomes `complete`, and the status of
   the design becomes `complete` or superseded.

A small task skips the design, and it can skip the plan. No task skips the
decision record when it makes an architectural choice.
